survey_growth_note: Close-approach counts are from the JPL CAD catalog and include approaches that happened before an object was discovered, so the history rises as surveys improve. Mercury, Venus, and Mars are counted within 0.05 AU. Jupiter is counted within 1 AU: 0.05 AU has only a handful of Jupiter encounters since 1900. Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto are listed from a 10 AU query and are not trained. Saturn and Uranus have a few public rows at every cutoff of 2 AU and wider, and Neptune and Pluto have none. Discovery counts by orbit class measure survey effort. The discovery regression uses the number of objects of that class known before the month. Comet perihelia in the training series are passages stepped from each comet's osculating perihelion and period, kept only when first_obs is on or before the passage. Periods outside 100 days to 200 years contribute only the single osculating passage. Earth-planet distances are JPL Horizons ephemerides; the network is a statistical extrapolation and is scored against that ephemeris on the outlook months. CAD times are TDB. Horizons observer times are UT. Moon discovery years come from the JPL satellite table and are not trained, because only a year is known. The IMO shower calendar was not a usable ZHR table when this feed was built, so no shower forecast is invented.

series.title: Comet perihelia known at the time
